A production 64-bit out-of-order CPU running Linux at 2 GHz is far beyond the scale and performance supported by this small sky130 flow and one Tiny Tapeout tile. Tapeout readiness today cannot be promised without implementation and verification.
Next action: Confirm the reduced processor scope before proceeding to interface definition and implementation; evaluate area, timing, and physical verification with the design tools afterward.
Proposed reduced spec: Propose an 8-bit multicycle in-order processor with four registers, arithmetic and logic operations, conditional branches, and a bounded 16-instruction program store. Use a serialized interface for program loading and observable execution results. This replaces 64-bit out-of-order execution and Linux support with a small bare-metal instruction set, and replaces 2 GHz with a provisional 50 MHz target. Retain one Tiny Tapeout tile as a goal subject to implementation checks, and replace today's tapeout-ready deadline with staged design and verification.

decision.rationale: 18 policy wins and +16 overall successes on this fixed DEV cohort; clear typed public decisions before RTL/EDA.
decision.disclose: Hardware completions fall by two net (4 paired regressions, 2 improvements); retain scope behavior without calling hardware generation more reliable.
decision.next_priority: Canonical actionable diagnostics, spec-correct independent test setup, effective bounded recovery, and cheaper stage memory before a separately frozen rerun.

limitations: DEV-only 30 cases × 3 stochastic repeats; no held-out assessment or significance claim.
Model outputs and initial implementations vary between cohorts; hardware delta does not isolate a deterministic causal effect of the gate.
Finite own/hidden test passes do not establish universal correctness or physical completion.
One I2C case per repeat explicitly tests upstream implementation compatibility; it is not a claim about arbitrary I2C architectures.
All three I2C current-source hidden checks fail; own tests never reach protocol behavior, so a separate compatibility defect remains unlocalized.
No USD-cost target claim; all dollar observations are unknown.
63 completed blocks have measured DRC/LVS and bundles, not independently qualified Tiny Tapeout wrappers or shuttle readiness.
No runtime, grader, corpus, image, summary, raw record, or evidence manifest was changed during this analysis.
